rail_guard.text: Fort William Station, halfway along the West Highland Line and all its scenic nonsense. It's been voted among the most beautiful railway journeys in the world, and the trains are very nearly on time.
Hop aboard! The Wildlore rail runs to every station you've visited in Great Britain. Where to?

then.text: We had a call-out up Glenmoriston. Turned out it was just a walker who'd stopped to stare at a capercaillie for three hours. Can't blame him.
Clag's down on the Ben today. If you're heading up, take a compass, and turn back if you're unsure. Please.
Rain's on, so the burns'll be up. If a crossing looks dodgy, it is. The hill will still be there tomorrow.
Clear day on the Ben! It'll be busy up there. Sun cream, water and a jumper for the top.

else.text: {greeting} Ben Nevis is a big, kind hill with a bad temper in the mist. We go up in all weathers, so you don't have to.
The summit's covered in cloud about three days in four, and there's a cliff off the north side. Take a map, a torch and a plan. In that order.

then.text: Steam looks best in the rain, you know. Big white clouds of it. The Jacobite never looked so grand.
Can't see the train in this fog, but I can hear it. Seventy-four, if hearing counts. I'm counting it.
Last train's been and gone. I'll be back tomorrow. Same spot, same flask, same happy waving.

fw_spotter.text: The Jacobite leaves here for Mallaig, a steam train that puffs along the viaduct at Glenfinnan, the one in the films. I've seen it go by seventy-three times.
I've never been on it. It's about the looking, you see. I look. The train does the rest.

then.text: Rain gets in the whistle and it goes a bit gurgly. Folk think it's a new style. I let them.
Can't play in this wind. Every note blows off down Loch Linnhe. Somebody in Oban's getting a free concert.

fw_piper.text: I play the whistle in front of the shop. The pipers all have their own pitch and I don't argue with a piper.
The Ben Nevis Race is held every September. They run up and back down in about two hours. I'd take a bus. It's the same view, only drier.

then.text: Sunshine! Gran says that means we can see Ireland. I think she just means the shop over there.
It's raining again. Gran says Fort William gets more rain than anywhere. I think she's proud of that.
I'm meant to be home before the midges come out. They're coming out. Bye!

fw_kid.text: {greeting} I've climbed Ben Nevis, you know. Well, I've climbed the Pony Track a bit. It's very big. My legs said no.
My gran says on a clear day you can see Ireland from the top. She says that a lot. I think she just likes the idea.

fw_walker.text: Ben Nevis tomorrow, dawn start. Packed three flasks, two jackets and a very large Kendal mint cake.

then.text: Rain at sea level means snow on top. Brilliant. I'm packing a second pair of socks.

else.text: Clear sky tonight, they say. Go up early, before the cloud gets ideas.

fw_runner.text: I'm training for the Ben Race. Up and down the biggest hill in Britain, against the clock. Cheerful hobby, I know.
If you see me walking, I'm having a moment. Give me a minute and a flapjack.

fw_lochside.text: Up and down the loch front before breakfast. The mountains don't mind, and the midges are still asleep.

then.text: Look at that, not a cloud on the Ben. Go and tell the locals. They won't believe you.

else.text: Everything here is either on a hill or in a loch. I've decided that's a feature.

fw_camper.text: Pitched the tent by the river. A stag walked past at midnight and didn't even apologise.
Chippy, campsite, midge net. That's the holiday plan, and it's perfect.

fw_keeper.text: Fancy five shots at my goal? I'll lean one way and dive another if I'm feeling mean. Shinty is hard on keepers and harder on shins.

then.text: Good game. The lads say you hit it like a Highlander, which on this pitch is an insult and a medal.
You beat the keeper? Right, you're an honorary Camanachd lad. The Braes can have our blessing, and a letter for Calum.

else.text: Shinty, camanachd in Gaelic, is older than the Union and rougher than hurling's cousin. Prove you're worth a letter: beat the keeper at the goal over there. Five shots, and he leans the wrong way when he's feeling mean.
I'm the captain of the Fort William lads. Come back when you've seen the court in Inverness.

then.text: New footbridge over the burn, steel and a handrail. Whoever put it in, thank you. I used to be a wet-boots-at-three-in-the-morning woman.
The water horse is in somebody's team, they say. The ford's quiet. I keep my boots dry and my eyes open.

ct_kelpie_sign.text: There's a sign at the ford now, and a rope. It says no, and in smaller print it says there may be a horse. I'm not crossing.

ct_kelpie_bridled.text: There's a bridle on the estate office wall that's never dry. I try not to look at it. It isn't looking at me, but I have my doubts.
